events.credibility_reason: A search summary says Barvinok and Ghomi called it 'highly original but flawed'; the record did not confirm this.

Anonymous, undated packet on a platform with no review; classes not defined; computations 'reported unreproduced' with script missing; dependencies self-described as 'incomplete'; the page itself says 'not proof evidence'; no uptake or citation.

Repository's own status is conflicting ('The full n=6 case remains unproved' vs all seven types written); several items listed as open may be premises; earlier reductions were refuted; only a self-review that disclaims being an audit.
events.ai_basis: The account below preserves Claude's prior work and chronology.

why: The statement asks whether every convex polyhedron (unstretched, actual edges) has a non-overlapping edge unfolding. Pseudo-edge, affine-stretch, topologically-convex/non-convex, and overlapping-unfolding results answer changed questions and are variants; Shiota et al. counts are finite instances; O'Rourke 2026 adds no class (none). Restricted convex classes (nearly flat caps, nested prismatoids, prismatoid subclasses, Hamiltonian-quasigeodesic polyhedra, polar zonohedra, convex polytopes with at most six vertices) are cases. The O'Rourke 2025 combinatorial paper has only a year-2025 journal date with a possibly earlier arXiv version, so it is placed null; it is a variant regardless. The six-vertex repository is a case claimed by an established researcher (Langerman, per the slef.org link) but internally inconsistent: doubtful, not set aside. Its AI role is the close call: Co-Authored-By trailers on commits that include the 'rotation-picture argument' and HANDOFF's statement that it 'preserves Claude's prior work' indicate the model produced part of the proof work, so assisted rather than none, though no step is itemised. ProofAtlas is set aside as not credible: anonymous, self-described as incomplete and not proof evidence, with unreproduced computations.
doubts: AI role for slef-2026 rests on commit trailers and one generic sentence; which proof steps Claude Fable 5.1 produced is unstated, and 'none' is a defensible alternative if the model's work was code and notes only. The Akitaya 2019 fewer-than-6 claim, if it covers convex polytopes, would be a pre-snapshot case, but it is unverified and the paper's main content is non-convex. Whether ProofAtlas's 'triangular reciprocal types' even correspond to a class of convex polyhedra is not established.
